title: A clean near-gap window does not validate the whole GW band set
symptom: hBN: the K/Gamma conduction-valley order is inverted vs plane-wave reference and high states show GW-PBE up to ~416 eV; WSe2 high-energy branches off by ~262 eV; MnF2 keeps X/M conduction kinks after the Vxc fix; SrTiO3 fails the QP root at state 30; GeTe GW gap is +0.17 eV vs literature but the CBM valley order differs.
root_cause: Near-gap acceptance criteria never exercised the full spectrum: valley order, root finding at high states, and band continuity are separate failure modes that a gap-only check cannot see.
minimal_fix: Accept a GW band set only when (a) the near-gap window matches its reference, (b) band extrema ORDER (valley positions) matches the reference within the same starting functional, (c) every reported QP state has a converged root, and (d) high-state corrections are finite and smoothly decaying. Report per-window verdicts instead of one gap number.
validation: Per-system numbers above define the bar; a figure that only crops the low-energy window must not be labelled as validated bands.
avoid: Claiming literature-level agreement from the gap value alone, mixing HSE with GW references, or ignoring SOC settings when quoting external numbers.

parameters.acceptance: near-gap window + valley order + converged roots + finite high states
